hook.text: Fourteen days of Play Tennis. On nine days they played. On five, they did not. A decision tree will predict the answer by asking one question at a time.

which.text: But which question comes first? Outlook, humidity, wind, or temperature?

idea.text: A good question leaves each group pure: all yes, or all no. Entropy measures how mixed a group is.

pure.text: A pure group, all one class, has entropy zero. There is nothing left to ask.

half.text: A fifty fifty group has entropy one bit. That is the worst case. You know nothing about the answer.

curve.text: In between, entropy climbs from zero to its peak at fifty fifty, and falls back to zero.

root.text: Our fourteen days, nine yes and five no, are quite mixed: zero point nine four zero bits.

split.text: Now try outlook. Sunny gets two yes and three no. Overcast gets four yes, and no no at all. Rain gets three yes and two no.

child.text: Overcast is pure: entropy zero. Sunny and rain are mixed: zero point nine seven one each.

weight.text: Weight each child by its size: five out of fourteen, four out of fourteen, five out of fourteen. Together they leave zero point six nine four.

gain.text: Entropy fell from zero point nine four zero to zero point six nine four. That drop, about zero point two four six, is the information gain.

others.text: Humidity would leave zero point seven eight eight. Wind, zero point eight nine two. Temperature, zero point nine one one. Outlook leaves the least, so outlook becomes the root.

rec.text: Then repeat inside every branch that is still mixed. Sunny asks about humidity. Rain asks about wind.

stop.text: The slides stop when a leaf holds a single example, or when splitting would raise the entropy.

prune.text: A tree grown too far starts to fit noise. Pruning cuts it back, and the tree is judged on new examples.

ex1.text: Entropy measures how mixed a node is.

ex2.text: Pure is zero. Fifty fifty is one bit, the worst.

ex3.text: Weight each child by its size.

ex4.text: Choose the split with the largest gain.
